 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The IMD World Competitiveness Center:**
 
 
• It is a research group at the **International Institute for Management Development (IMD)** located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**. It has been publishing these rankings annually since **1989**.
 
• The ranking is widely regarded as one of the most authoritative reports on the competitiveness of nations, focusing on how nations manage their resources and competencies to increase prosperity.
 
 
 
• **The Four Pillars of Competitiveness:**
 
 
• **Economic Performance:** Evaluates the domestic economy, **International Trade**, **International Investment**, **Employment**, and **Prices**.
 
• **Government Efficiency:** Measures **Public Finance**, **Tax Policy**, **Institutional Framework**, **Business Legislation**, and **Societal Framework**.
 
• **Business Efficiency:** Assesses **Productivity and Efficiency**, **Labor Market**, **Finance**, **Management Practices**, and **Attitudes and Values**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** Looks at **Basic Infrastructure**, **Technological Infrastructure**, **Scientific Infrastructure**, **Health and Environment**, and **Education**.
 
 
 
• **Methodology and Data:**
 
 
• The ranking utilizes a combination of **Hard Data** (representing about **two-thirds** of the weight), which includes statistical indicators from international and national sources, and **Soft Data** (representing **one-third** of the weight) from an **Executive Opinion Survey**.
 
• In **2025**, the criteria were updated to reflect emerging global trends such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption**, **Energy Security**, and **Geopolitical Stability**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Global Markets:**
 
 
• Economies like **Denmark**, **Ireland**, and **Sweden** often fluctuate within the top ten, highlighting the competitive nature of **European** markets compared to **Asian** powerhouses.
 
• The **2025** rankings specifically highlighted how "small" economies often outperform larger ones like the **USA** or **China** due to their **Agility** and specialized **Economic Policies**.
 
 
</ul

__ 
 
• The **10th Sustainable Development Report** (SDR), released in **2025**, provides an updated assessment of the progress made by all **United Nations** member states toward the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• According to the report, **India** achieved an overall score of **67** out of **100**. This score indicates India's percentage of total progress toward achieving the **17 SDGs**.
 
• The report is published annually by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. The **2025** edition marks a decade since the world adopted the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development** in **September 2015**.
 
• India’s score of **67** reflects steady progress in certain areas, such as **Goal 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)** and **Goal 13 (Climate Action)**, although it also highlights sectors that require urgent attention to meet the **2030** deadline.
 
• The **SDG Index** score is a composite measure that aggregates data across all **17 goals**, providing a clear picture of where a country stands in its development journey compared to the ideal target of **100**.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 
 
 
• The **SDGs**, also known as the **Global Goals**, were adopted by all **193 UN Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that all people enjoy peace and prosperity by **2030**.
 
• There are **17 Goals** and **169 Targets** that are integrated and indivisible, balancing the three dimensions of sustainable development: the **economic**, **social**, and **environmental**.
 
 
 
• **SDSN and the Report:** 
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** has been operating under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** since **2012**.
 
• The report is led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs** and uses a rigorous methodology to rank countries based on their distance from the **SDG** targets.
 
 
 
• **India's Internal Monitoring:** 
 
 
• In **India**, the **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring the **SDGs**. It released the first **SDG India Index** in **2018** to foster competition among states.
 
• States like **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, and **Himachal Pradesh** have consistently emerged as top performers in the domestic **SDG** rankings.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in 2025:** 
 
 
• The **2025 report** emphasizes that the "SDG stimulus" is crucial, as many developing nations face a massive financing gap. High-income countries like **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** usually top the global index with scores exceeding **80**.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate among youth aged 15-29 in rural areas in May 2025, as per the PLFS?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.7%**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is a critical survey conducted by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** to estimate key employment and unemployment indicators.
 
• As per the data released for **May 2025**, the **unemployment rate** for the **youth** population, specifically those in the **age group of 15-29 years**, was a focal point of the report.
 
• In **rural areas**, the **unemployment rate** for this specific youth demographic was recorded at **13.7%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 13.7%.***
 
• The **Unemployment Rate (UR)** is defined as the percentage of persons unemployed among the persons in the **labour force** (which includes both employed persons and those seeking work).
 
• The **PLFS** serves as a primary source of **data** for the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** to monitor the health of the **Indian economy** and the effectiveness of employment schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2017**, the **PLFS** was established to provide more frequent and reliable **labour force data**.
 
• It has two main objectives: to estimate employment indicators in **Current Weekly Status (CWS)** every three months for **urban areas** and to estimate indicators in both **Usual Status** and **CWS** annually for both **rural** and **urban areas**.
 
 
 
• **Key Definitions:**
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** The percentage of the population that is either working or seeking work.
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** The percentage of employed persons in the total population.
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR):** The percentage of those in the **labour force** who are currently without work but available for and seeking it.
 
 
 
• **Youth Demographics:**
 
 
• In the context of Indian **government surveys** and the **National Youth Policy**, **youth** is generally defined as persons in the **age group of 15-29 years**.
 
• Monitoring this specific group is essential for addressing **skill development** needs and reducing **demographic** pressures on the **job market**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Measurement Status:**
 
 
• **Usual Status (ps+ss):** This determines the employment status of a person based on a reference period of **365 days** preceding the date of the survey.
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):** This determines the status based on a reference period of **7 days** preceding the survey date. A person is considered employed if they worked for at least **one hour** on any day during the reference week.
 
 
 
• **Organizational Framework:**
 
 
• The **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• Data collected through these surveys influences major policy decisions related to **MGNREGA**, **Skill India**, and other **social security** initiatives.
 
 
</ul
